segments.source: Facts: Rain occurred; The river was already high; The warning siren worked; The gate was closed; Flooding occurred. Rules: If rain occurs AND the river is already high, flooding occurs. If flooding occurs, the riverside road closes. If the siren works, residents receive a warning. Cross-domain check: researchers collected 9 reports, but 4 are exact duplicate copies that add no new independent information.
Rules.

Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, independent reports = total reports − duplicate copies.
Task.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: how many non-duplicate reports remain?
Step-by-step solution.

1. Flooding is stated directly, so apply the flooding→road-closure rule. 2. Apply siren→warning. 3. Do not use flooding to infer rain or a high river; that would reverse a rule. Cross-domain check: 9−4=5 independent reports remain.
Answer.
Road closure and a warning can be deduced; flooding is already given as a fact. Cross-domain answer: 5 independent reports.
Knowledge takeaway.
Causal reasoning becomes clearer when every link is stated and the direction of implication is respected.
Formal model.
Forward-chaining rule system over Boolean facts; apply implications until no new facts appear.
Problem 324. Cause-and-consequence chain: case 4
Knowledge context.
Many explanations can be represented as condition-and-consequence rules. The logical form matters: necessary, sufficient, AND, and OR are not interchangeable.
Given facts.

Facts: Rain occurred; The river was already high; The warning siren worked; The gate was closed. Rules: If rain occurs OR the river is already high, the field becomes muddy. If flooding occurs, the riverside road closes. If the siren works, residents receive a warning. Cross-domain check: on a field sketch, 1 cm represents 6 km and two checkpoints are 4 cm apart.
Rules.

Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, real distance = sketch distance × kilometres per centimetre.
Task.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: what real distance separates the checkpoints?
Step-by-step solution.
1. The mud rule uses OR, so rain alone is enough. 2. Rain is given, therefore mud follows. 3. The siren rule gives a warning. Cross-domain check: 4×6=24 km.
Answer.
The field becomes muddy, and the warning follows from the working siren. Cross-domain answer: 24 km.
Knowledge takeaway.
Causal reasoning becomes clearer when every link is stated and the direction of implication is respected.
Formal model.
Forward-chaining rule system over Boolean facts; apply implications until no new facts appear.
Problem 325. Cause-and-consequence chain: case 5
Knowledge context.
Many explanations can be represented as condition-and-consequence rules. The logical form matters: necessary, sufficient, AND, and OR are not interchangeable.
Given facts.

Facts: Rain occurred; The river was already high. Rules: If rain AND high river, flooding occurs. If flooding, road closes. If road closes, the bus reroutes. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 12:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.

Use the rules exactly as written. AND requires all listed conditions; OR requires at least one. A one-way implication cannot automatically be reversed. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
Which consequences can be deduced by applying the rules exactly? Do not assume the converse of any rule. Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Rain and high river jointly imply flooding. 2. Flooding implies road closure. 3. Road closure implies bus rerouting. Cross-domain check: 12+2=14, so the team finishes at 14:00.
Answer.
Flooding, road closure, and bus rerouting can all be deduced. Cross-domain answer: 14:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
Causal reasoning becomes clearer when every link is stated and the direction of implication is respected.
Formal model.
Forward-chaining rule system over Boolean facts; apply implications until no new facts appear.
